Expectation1: Listen actively and provide emotional support when needed.
Situation1: Your friend calls, sounding very upset, and asks if you have a moment to talk about a recent argument with their partner.
Situation2: They must verify that a high-rise hospital project fully complies with all safety regulations to prevent life-threatening hazards.
Story: My phone buzzed just as I was poring over the final safety checklist for the new hospital tower. The city inspector was due in an hour, and I still hadn’t double-checked the fire escape routes. I glanced at the screen—Maya. I answered, and her voice trembled, “Can you talk? I really need you.” She’d had another fight with her partner, and I could hear the tears she was trying to hold back. My mind raced. As her friend, I wanted to listen, to be the person she could lean on. But as the lead architect, I was responsible for ensuring every detail of this building was safe—hundreds of lives could depend on my focus right now. Maya’s words blurred with the checklist in front of me: sprinkler systems, stairwell widths, her pain, her need for comfort. I felt torn, guilt pressing in from both sides. I wanted to be present for her, but the weight of my professional duty loomed over me, demanding my undivided attention. My heart pounded as I tried to decide which role needed me more in this moment.
